gen-dafont-visitor-gf-nobile: Nobile reads tight and tidy, its caps sitting close to the lowercase and its letter mouths left open like unjoined chalk arcs. Line after line, this sans stays quiet beneath the bent-wire strokes of Visitor.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-nokora: Clean and approachable, Nokora lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase. Visitor's rod-stock strokes, identical in thickness across horizontals and verticals, give Nokora's never-tightening s something sturdy to lean against.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam reads tall and full, its curve endings kept apart. Visitor is a nostalgic display face with no pinched joins or swelling bowls, which leaves this plain sans plenty of room to talk.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Visitor's gaping e mouths and strokes pulled like solder give it an unmistakable digital, nostalgic bite. And Noto Sans Armenian settles underneath, tall and full in the lowercase, so extended text stays approachable.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Visitor brings gaping e mouths and short ascenders over big bowls, a nostalgic, digital look. But Noto Sans Avestan adds curve tips that never touch and a pronounced x-height, so the two share a page easily.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-bassa-va: Nostalgic from the first glance, Visitor holds one constant pen width throughout, like bent wire. Yet Noto Sans Bassa Vah fills the line with a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c, which keeps running text smooth.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cham: Wiry and a bit retro, Visitor draws a rope-thin outline with no thick or thin parts, all gaping e mouths. Visitor grabs attention; Noto Sans Cham, tall and rounded, carries the text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Retro and digital in one glance: Visitor has gaping e mouths and no thick-thin swing. Noto Sans Cherokee, a tall band of letters under short stalks, stays approachable across a full page of text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Nostalgic through and through, Visitor squeezes out one steady line like toothpaste. Noto Sans Chorasmian, with curves that stop short and a large x-height, keeps longer reading comfortable and contemporary.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Noto Sans Cuneiform swells its lowercase like inflated glass beads, with an e that opens up instead of closing. Visitor's parallel-edged strokes do the shouting; the sans does the talking.
